speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) in the past three years, how many individuals have leveraged on the Global Investor Programme and invested at least $2.5 million in a business, fund, or family office in order to qualify for permanent residency; and (b) what steps has the Government taken to facilitate their integration and eventual conversion to Singapore Citizenship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Permanent Residents (PRs) under the GIP can join other new residents in Singapore in various integration activities organised by the National Integration Council (NIC) and partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, the People’s Association Integration Council conducts the Heartland Orientation Trail to give participants an immersive experience of our heartlands and the Singapore way of life and help them understand and appreciate our local culture and norms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: New PRs under the GIP are also able to tap on the Economic Development Board (EDB)’s networks to embark on philanthropic activities or contribute to community causes that benefit our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: All applicants for Singapore Citizenship, including PRs under the GIP, are assessed independently by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For the individuals under the Global Investor Programme, which sectors are the businesses or investments in?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And what is the total investment amount that they have brought in over the last three years?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Mr Yip Hon Weng for his two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He asked about the investment over the last three years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have on hand, the numbers from 2011 to 2022, over an 11-year period.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the first question on sectors, I must say that GIP investors come from a wide spectrum of areas and sectors like technology, urban solutions and sustainability as well as financial services.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to use this occasion to reassure the Member Mr Yip and the House that EDB conducts regular reviews to ensure rootedness by the GIP investors in Singapore and that they contribute to our industries, to our economy and to job creation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, the GIP PRs are required to submit documentary evidence of the Singapore-based companies that they have invested in.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition to looking through all the documentary evidence, EDB will also conduct site visits to assess the companies' business activities and the employment situation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a quick question to the Minister of State vis-à-vis her response to the hon Member Mr Yip.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For the GIP individuals who are PRs, does EDB or the Ministry track how many of them transit to being citizens in view of her reply to Mr Yip's question on rootedness?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As you can see, we are very selective about the GIP investors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The EDB evaluation process is very stringent and very robust.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will look at their economic commitments as well as residency commitments.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to use this occasion to just elaborate on what I mentioned earlier about us requiring the GIP investor to submit documentary evidence and EDB mounting site visits to validate the numbers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to say that the PRs in GIP who do not meet the GIP economic and residency commitments as well as other renewable criteria will not have their re-entry permit renewed.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I think all Members in the House would know this is serious because once your re-entry permit is not renewed, this means that when the GIP PR subsequently leaves Singapore or if he or she remains overseas without a valid re-entry permit, their PR status will lapse; they will lose their PR status.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just confirm if the small percentage that the Minister of State speaks of is a number that she has on hand?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And would the Government be prepared to release that number?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I would elaborate and say that the interest in the GIP has remained stable since its launch.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the question about Singapore Citizenship, like I mentioned, the number of GIP PRs granted citizenship is even much lesser, as the Member can see from the PR numbers that have been granted over the past three years.
